title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries

reading.body:
An AI-powered delivery system was deployed to manage kitchen operations at Pizza Hut franchise locations in 2024. The system, called Dragontail, gave third-party delivery drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, which created an operational failure: drivers began waiting to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately, extending delivery times significantly.

The system was used in conditions it was not built to handle. The franchise had operated with over 90% on-time delivery before deployment, suggesting kitchen and delivery processes were already functioning. The AI's visibility into operations created a new bottleneck rather than solving an existing problem. Sales metrics deteriorated markedly after rollout, with growth reversing to decline in major markets.

A lawsuit has been filed alleging over $100 million in damages and that Pizza Hut ignored worsening performance data while enforcing continued use of the system. Whether Pizza Hut's actions constitute negligence or breach of contract is not established and remains a matter for legal proceedings.

Frustrated franchisee sues Pizza Hut over crappy kitchen AI
A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries

summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas claiming the chain's new AI-powered delivery system caused over $100 million in damages to its business. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, alleges that the Dragontail platform created significant operational problems after being implemented in 2024. The system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately. This resulted in longer delivery times, reduced customer satisfaction, and sharp sales declines.

Before Dragontail's rollout, Chaac maintained over 90% on-time delivery and double-digit sales growth. After implementation, the franchisee saw dramatic performance drops, including New York City sales swinging from positive 10.19% growth to negative 9.78%. Chaac alleges Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training or support and ignored worsening metrics while forcing continued use of the problematic software. The franchisee is seeking over $100 million in damages plus attorneys' fees. Pizza Hut declined to comment beyond stating it would respond through appropriate legal channels.
